questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VII, Section 704(1)(c), eaves over required windows must be at least how many millimeters from the side and rear property lines?

600 mm
700 mm
750 mm

questions.rationale: Section 704(1)(c) requires eaves over required windows to be not less than 750 millimeters from the side and rear property lines. This is a narrow rule: it governs only eaves over required windows on side and rear lines, not all projections or all facades.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VII, Section 704(1)(a), no building may be constructed unless it has what minimum relationship to a public space, yard, or street?

It must adjoin or have direct access to a public space, yard, or street on at least one of its sides
It must adjoin a public space on at least two opposite sides
It must have frontage on a public street equal to at least half of its perimeter

questions.rationale: Section 704(1)(a) is the basic location rule: no building shall be constructed unless it adjoins or has direct access to a public space, yard, or street on at least one of its sides. Direct frontage on a public street is not required; access through an easement or yard is sufficient.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VII, Sec. 704(1)(c), eaves over required windows must be at least how many millimeters from side and rear property lines?

750 mm

questions.rationale: The 750 mm applies specifically to eaves over required windows on side and rear lines. Front yard setbacks are governed by local zoning ordinances and Rule VII Sec. 702-703.

Buildings on the same property are automatically considered one building if they share a common wall, provided the wall meets fire-resistance ratings

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VII Section 704, when a building is constructed with its exterior wall directly on a side or rear property line (zero setback on that side), what opening and wall requirement applies to that wall?

options.text: The wall must be constructed as a firewall with no unprotected openings permitted at zero setback from the property line
Openings are permitted up to 50 percent of the wall area as long as fire-rated glazing is used
Openings are permitted up to 25 percent of the wall area, with no special fire-rating required
Openings are unrestricted because zero-setback walls are governed by local zoning, not PD 1096

questions.rationale: A wall built on the property line presents maximum fire-spread risk to the adjacent property. Section 704 therefore requires the wall to be a firewall, and no unprotected openings are permitted in an exterior wall located at zero setback from the property line.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VII, Section 704, when an exterior wall opening requires protection, what is the maximum percentage of the total wall area in any storey that may be occupied by protected openings?

33 percent of the wall area in that storey
50 percent of the wall area in that storey
75 percent of the wall area in that storey

questions.rationale: Section 704 limits the sum of protected openings in an exterior wall in any storey to a maximum of 50 percent of the total wall area in that storey. The wall-area basis is per storey, not the whole building.

questions.text: For purposes of measuring distances under PD 1096 Rule VII, Section 704(1)(b), how is the adjacent property line established when a building adjoins a street or alley?

At the centerline of the adjoining street or alley
At the near edge (face of curb) of the street or alley
At the legal lot boundary only, regardless of street or alley

questions.rationale: Section 704(1)(b) provides that, for purposes of this section, the centerline of an adjoining street or alley shall be considered an adjacent property line when applying the exterior-wall and opening-protection rules in Section 704.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VII, Section 704, two or more buildings on the same property may be treated as one building only if which condition is met?

Their aggregate area does not exceed the allowable floor area for a single building, and the most restrictive occupancy and construction requirements are applied
They are located on separately titled lots that are consolidated by permit for the sole purpose of parking
They have identical heights and footprints, and each is provided with independent means of egress

questions.rationale: Section 704 allows two or more buildings on the same property to be treated as one building only if their aggregate area is within the allowable floor area for a single building; where occupancy groups or construction types differ, the most restrictive requirements govern.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VII, Section 704, what is the maximum projection beyond an exterior wall, expressed as a fraction of the distance from the assumed vertical plane (where opening protection first becomes required) to the property line?

options.text: One-fourth (1/4) of the distance
One-third (1/3) of the distance
One-half (1/2) of the distance
Two-thirds (2/3) of the distance

questions.rationale: Section 704 limits projections beyond the exterior wall to a maximum of one-third of the distance from the assumed vertical plane where opening protection first becomes required to the property line. The distance is measured at right angles from the property line.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Sec. 704, when a building wall faces the centerline of a street, alley, or public way, how is the property line treated for setback calculations?

The centerline of the street, alley, or public way is treated as the property line
The property line is treated as the far edge of the street right-of-way
No setback is required when a building faces a public right-of-way centerline

questions.rationale: Sec. 704 establishes that when a building faces a street, alley, or public way, the centerline of that right-of-way is treated as the property line for the purpose of calculating fire separation distances and setback requirements.

An imaginary property line is drawn at the midpoint between the two buildings, 2 meters from each wall
No fire separation distance applies because both buildings are on the same lot, allowing for unrestricted design flexibility.
The fire separation distance is measured from each building to the nearest actual property line, which may vary depending on lot configuration.

questions.rationale: Sec. 704 requires that when two buildings on the same lot face each other, an imaginary property line is established at the midpoint between them. Each building's exterior wall opening limits are then calculated as if this imaginary line were the actual property line.

questions.text: An exterior wall on a side property line contains windows totaling 4.2 sq.m in a storey where the total wall face area is 9 sq.m. Does this opening percentage comply with PD 1096 Sec. 704, assuming the wall is set back 1.0 meter from the property line?

options.text: Compliant: 4.2/9 = 46.7%, which is below the 50% maximum for unprotected openings
Non-compliant: at 1.0m setback, the allowable opening percentage is reduced below 50%
Compliant: window area is calculated against gross floor area, not wall area
Non-compliant: 4.2 sq.m exceeds the absolute maximum of 4.0 sq.m per storey per face

questions.rationale: 4.2 sq.m of openings in a 9 sq.m wall face equals 46.7%, which is below the 50% maximum set by Sec. 704. At a 1.0m setback, the 50% limit applies; no separate reduction is specified for this setback distance in the base code provision.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Sec. 704, when a building wall faces the centerline of a street, alley, or public way, how is the property line treated for setback calculations?

options.text: The property line is measured from the building face to the street edge nearest the lot
The centerline of the street, alley, or public way is treated as the property line
The property line is treated as the far edge of the street right-of-way
No setback is required when a building faces a public right-of-way centerline

questions.rationale: Sec. 704 establishes that when a building faces a street, alley, or public way, the centerline of that right-of-way is treated as the property line for the purpose of calculating fire separation distances and setback requirements.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Sec. 704, what is the maximum percentage of an exterior wall area per storey that may contain unprotected openings (windows, doors, vents)?

options.text: 30% maximum unprotected openings per exterior wall face per storey
40% maximum unprotected openings per exterior wall face per storey
50% maximum unprotected openings per exterior wall face per storey
60% maximum unprotected openings per exterior wall face per storey

questions.rationale: Sec. 704 limits unprotected openings in exterior walls to a maximum of 50% of the wall area per storey per face. This limit controls the amount of unprotected glass or open area through which fire could spread between buildings.

questions.text: An exterior wall projection (such as a bay window or balcony) extends toward a side property line. Under PD 1096 Sec. 704, what is the maximum projection permitted as a fraction of the distance between the building wall and the property line?

options.text: Projections may not exceed one-quarter of the distance to the property line
Projections may not exceed one-third of the distance to the property line
Projections may not exceed one-half of the distance to the property line
Projections may not exceed two-thirds of the distance to the property line

questions.rationale: Sec. 704 limits exterior wall projections (bay windows, balconies, canopies) to a maximum of one-third of the distance between the building wall and the property line, ensuring a minimum fire separation clearance is maintained.

questions.text: A building's side wall is located 1.5 meters from the property line with a projection (covered walkway canopy) extending 0.6 meters toward the property line. Does this projection comply with PD 1096 Sec. 704?

options.text: Compliant: 0.6m is less than half the 1.5m setback, satisfying the one-third rule
Non-compliant: 0.6m exceeds one-third of the 1.5m setback distance (maximum 0.5m)
Compliant: covered walkway canopies are exempt from the projection limits in Sec. 704
Non-compliant: projections are prohibited within 1.5m of a property line regardless of size

questions.rationale: The one-third rule limits projections to a maximum of 1/3 × 1.5m = 0.5m. The proposed 0.6m projection exceeds this limit by 0.1m and does not comply with Sec. 704.

questions.text: Two buildings on the same compound are 6 meters apart facing each other. Building A has a 3-storey wall with 60% unprotected openings per storey on the face toward Building B. Evaluate this opening percentage against PD 1096 Sec. 704 requirements.

options.text: Compliant: the imaginary property line is 3m from Building A, and 60% openings are permitted at 3m setback
Non-compliant: 60% exceeds the 50% maximum regardless of separation distance from the imaginary property line
Compliant: same-lot buildings are exempt from the exterior wall opening limits in Sec. 704
Non-compliant: the imaginary property line is at 3m, and openings exceeding 50% require protected assemblies

questions.rationale: The imaginary property line is drawn at the midpoint — 3 meters from Building A. At 3 meters from an (imaginary) property line, the 50% maximum unprotected opening limit still applies. Building A's 60% opening ratio exceeds this limit. To comply, the openings must either be reduced to 50% or replaced with protected (fire-rated) glazing assemblies.
